decisions.reason: SOL keeps the sense of moving as one while tightening the phrasing.

SOL keeps the red vision image in natural wording.

SOL drops the energy’s surging motion from the source.
SOL preserves the wall being partly torn down in more direct phrasing.

SOL keeps the image and trims an unnecessary phrase.

SOL preserves the scope of his gaze and the names’ power to make the world tremble.

SOL keeps the loss of sight and hearing and the destruction of everything in the shock wave’s reach.

SOL preserves both the continuing power and the fact that he unleashed the calamity.
SOL keeps his turn toward the area beyond the dust and silence.

SOL keeps the Disciple’s ongoing mark on the world in natural phrasing.

SOL adds that he swung the spearhead to meet the attack, an action not stated in the source.
SOL preserves the glance and faint smile while avoiding a cumbersome sentence.
SOL clearly states that deflecting the attack confirmed his standing above the Three Saints.
The em dash preserves the source’s alternative labels for the realm.
The source describes a concentrated mass of light; SOL changes it into multiple masses.
“Them” clearly refers to the barrage of light and avoids needless repetition.
“A lot might have turned out differently” matches the source’s plain “much” more naturally than SOL’s “much might.”
The source explicitly says they went unnoticed by the North Heaven Demon Lord; BASE preserves that referent.
SOL preserves their haste and lack of proper rest before battle.
The source calls it a guess, not a deduction.
SOL preserves the attacks bouncing off his concentrated Force and his heightened exhilaration.

SOL turns the fragment into a clear sentence without changing the power’s effect.
The source says no one had imagined a human could possess this energy; SOL narrows that to what he imagined.
The following direct thought makes the omitted “thinking” attribution clear.
The source says it felt as though he could do anything; SOL removes that hedge.
The italic emphasis preserves the correction from feeling able to being able.
The referent is clear, and SOL preserves his senses enveloping the gorge.
SOL preserves the Sound Transmission exchange and the unsettled dust cloud.
SOL drops the speaker’s emphatic claim about how handsome and clever his “little guy” is.
“Waistband” naturally renders 바지춤 without changing the physical action.
“Gaze darkened” and the following description preserve his reaction.
The source says he must have gotten lucky; SOL changes that into a “lucky guess.”
“Try moving to the side” keeps the request and its anxious tone.
The source says “touch this old man’s body”; SOL replaces the physical action with the idiom “lay a hand.”
The source says “that’s not a hand”; SOL adds “my,” changing the joke’s setup.
The source explicitly marks the moment his mouth twitches.
The next line corrects the claim that silence descended; SOL preemptively makes it seem to descend and repeats the correction.
SOL’s short correction works with the preceding sentence’s “seemed.”
The added conjunction keeps the speaker’s observation and preserves the meaning.
The source says he had definitely identified them; SOL changes this to ongoing guessing.
SOL keeps the dismissive challenge and the bet on Hyuk’s balls.
“Tap” better matches the source’s 툭 than SOL’s sharper “snap.”
SOL preserves the breaking patience and cold voice in direct prose.
“I don’t know who he is” naturally preserves the source’s “whoever that is.”
SOL keeps the emergence, shoulder-brushing action, and reply while combining them smoothly.
The reply is retained in the preceding hunk, so deleting this duplicate span loses no source content.
SOL preserves the embarrassed remark and the Disciple’s relative height.
The source says he should stake his own; SOL’s “stake those” is less clear and weakens the punchline.
“That’s crossing a line” keeps the rebuke and the interrupted reply.
“The rest of his words” preserves that the crash cuts off the unfinished line.
“A moment later” naturally preserves the brief delay before the cough.
SOL changes the fine dust into smog and says the man brought it, altering the physical joke.
“Stop making a fuss” naturally conveys the rebuke against exaggerating.
“My God” preserves the exasperated force of 세상에 better than SOL’s milder “Seriously.”
“Gaze darkened” naturally conveys his sinking, darkening look.
SOL preserves the reduced attack strength, the evasion, and the inference that they had strength in reserve.
The source says this realization came at some point; SOL drops that temporal detail.
SOL keeps the realization that he underestimated his enemies.
The speaker is clear from context, and SOL preserves the hunting-dog characterization.
“Won’t stand by any longer” conveys that they will no longer wait and watch.
“Use every force we have” preserves the order to commit all their forces.
The source specifies that Jamukha understood the order to use their full strength; SOL omits that detail.
“The whole game was overturned” preserves the source’s sense of the battle being upended more naturally than “the whole board.”
SOL preserves using every available means in cleaner phrasing.
“As you command” keeps the subordinate’s formal assent.
SOL preserves pulling the flare from his robes and yanking its cord.
“Shot up” keeps the smoke rising into the night with a brisker verb.
SOL preserves the Bow Saint’s arrows dispersing most of the smoke and the remaining wisps escaping her.
The source describes the sky as blackened; BASE retains that image.
SOL preserves Jamukha releasing his subordinates and taking the pill he had been stopped from using.
